JOURNAL

Where the sound comes from

2026.09.16

People often ask where the inspiration comes from. Honestly, it's rarely something "found" — most of the time it's stumbled into: an old song playing halfway through on a radio down the street, a stranger's offhand line while paying at a convenience store, the rhythm of rain hitting a tin roof.

Cities are actually pretty loud, but if you're willing to listen, all sorts of small, scattered melodies are hiding inside the noise. Yu Stellar has a habit of writing these moments down — sometimes in full sentences, sometimes just an adjective, like "a rain-soaked streetlamp" or "a goodnight said too late." Later, when it's time to write, it means going back through these notes to see which word is still glowing.

So rather than saying a song gets "created," it might be more accurate to say the scattered fragments of everyday life get rearranged into a sentence. Inspiration is always there — it's just often too quiet, and easy to miss.
